title: How the screening room is built
question: Third hand — everything from the first two rounds is eliminated. The roll led with Three Rooms. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Three Rooms
options.lineage: a clinic visit — you are prepared somewhere, tested somewhere, told somewhere
options.thesis: Three named places, each with exactly one job, and you always know which one you are standing in.
options.viewport: A single quiet room filling the screen, named at the top, holding only what that room is for.
options.case: The product already has a bright room and a dim room; naming the places makes the existing threshold into the navigation rather than an effect.
options.risk: Three rooms is three transitions, and every transition is motion you owe the user an excuse for.

options.label: The Curtain
options.lineage: a darkened exam room where only the thing being looked at is lit
options.thesis: The screen is dark and only what you need this second is lit; everything else is not dimmed, it is simply not there.
options.viewport: Near-black, with a single line of instruction and the target lit above it, and nothing else on screen at all.
options.case: Light hurts and attention is scarce, so the least photophobic and least distracting interface is the one that renders almost nothing — and it makes the stimulus the only bright thing, which is exactly what the measurement needs.
options.risk: An interface that hides its own controls can leave a foggy user unable to find the way out — the stop action can never be hidden.

regions.label: the target, the only bright thing

options.label: The Chart Wall
options.lineage: the eye chart on the far wall of every optometrist's room
options.thesis: The whole viewport is one calibrated field, and each task is a position and a scale within it rather than a separate screen.
options.viewport: One measured wall filling the screen, marked like an instrument, with the current task living somewhere on it.
options.case: Nothing ever navigates — the field is constant and only the target's position and scale change, which is the least disruptive way to move between seven tasks.
options.risk: A single field for seven different tasks risks reading as decoration rather than instrument, and vertical tasks fight a landscape screen.
